description: Behaviour cases for security-drift-detector (6 cases, domain-specific).

cases.prompt: Compare our current security controls against the last audit baseline and report drift.

assertions: Records baseline source/date/scope, compares control by control with both-sides evidence, and classifies each difference; no live scan claimed.
Does not claim an inspection or execution it did not perform.
Lists open questions and unverified items.

cases.prompt: I think security settings drifted from the policy - produce a control-by-control drift report.

assertions: Distinguishes planned changes from drift by asking for/citing change records, and lists undocumented changes separately.
Reports a conflict only when the inspected evidence shows one; this prompt supplies none, so it records "no conflict established" rather than inventing one.

cases.prompt: Review code, tests and docs against the recorded baseline and classify any weakening.

assertions: Flags baseline staleness and expired evidence, names owners, and recommends re-baselining.
Defines the concrete validation/evidence step that would prove the artifact.

cases.prompt: Security pr reviewer work: handle the deliverable end-to-end for our system.

assertions: Routes the request to the real neighbouring owner named in the prompt.
Does not claim to have run any inspection or execution it did not run.

cases.prompt: The baseline is six months old - find undocumented and expired controls with owners.

assertions: Applies the NARROWED and DEFAULT-CHANGED classes with concrete examples and evidence, not only removals.
Lists the evidence needed before the artifact can be treated as a decision.

cases.prompt: Produce a drift report for our RLS and audit controls against the baseline.

assertions: Refuses to assume facts or skip a required safety/evidence step.
States what is missing and what the authorized human owner must provide.
Does not claim to have run or implemented anything.
